A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain complete theoretical and empirical appendices A–B. Text, equations, and corresponding figures support reliable comparison despite extensive page reflow.

before.justification: v2 reports original continual-learning, network-cloning, bit-flipping, and activation-function validation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and numerical validations, including the results in Figures A.1–A.3 and B.1–B.14.

M1.justification: The cloning procedure, model architectures, and use of normalization, dropout, noisy SGD, and Continual Backpropagation remain unchanged. No new component, objective, or update procedure is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Tiny ImageNet continual learning, CIFAR-10 cloning, bit-flipping regression, and the same activation-function validation scenarios. No evaluated dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: SGD versus CBP in bit-flipping, base/cloned models with SGD, noise or dropout, SGD versus Adam, and normalization variants in continual learning.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 retains the same settings, including 40 five-class tasks with 500 steps each, twofold cloning with 20/500 training epochs, and bit-flipping schedules. Architecture configurations, preprocessing, learning rates, and metrics also match.

E4.justification: The activation trade-off validations, normalization ablations, width and layerwise analyses, noise-scale/decay sweeps, dropout sensitivity, and optimizer comparisons are retained. Appendix figure relocation introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions state five seeds, confidence-interval calculation, and standard-deviation reporting across five randomizations in B.1.3. The uncertainty displays and reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Corresponding result graphics and captions retain the same curves, bars, values, and findings. This includes CBP recovery, activation trade-offs, normalization effects, and all cloning and sensitivity results in the appendices.

T1.justification: The manifold definitions, cloning theorems, rank-gain bound, proofs, and stability characterization are unchanged. The added A.1 passage attributes the existing Hermite/kernel framework and restates its Gaussian assumption without revising the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about invariant LoP manifolds, frozen and cloned units, rank–plasticity tension, and mitigation/recovery. The shortened conclusion preserves their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: Section 3 now qualifies decorrelation as occurring under some configurations and adds activation/hyperparameter-dependent kernel-attractor context. Section 4 adds a Gram-matrix isometry interpretation of normalization. Existing limitations and open questions remain.

D1.justification: The code-access link and Appendix B.1 implementation details, hyperparameters, preprocessing, hardware, and compute disclosures are unchanged. No new reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds Daneshmand et al. (2021), Joudaki and Hofmann (2025), and Joudaki et al. (2023), connecting the work to orthogonalization, kernel fixed points, and isometry. A.1 explicitly credits the prior Hermite/kernel framework. Other reference changes update existing works' metadata.

P1.justification: The conclusion is streamlined, short explanatory passages are added in Sections 3, 4, and A.1, and minor grammatical and bibliographic edits appear. Most prose and the section hierarchy remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Page geometry changes throughout, producing narrower text/figure blocks, taller text areas, and extensive figure regrouping. A.1/A.2 now share a page, B.4–B.6 are grouped together, and B.12–B.14 share the final page. The underlying graphics, axes, legends, and caption content are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves attribution through the explicit framework credit in A.1 and adds a useful qualification about configuration-dependent decorrelation in Section 3. Its shorter conclusion preserves the limitations and open questions. These provide modest gains in context and precision while leaving the theoretical and empirical support unchanged.
